test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Oct 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some Ponds are Fishes.

Some Rivers are Fishes.

All Fishes are Tanks.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some Rivers are Tanks.

(II) Some Ponds are Rivers.
solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5eb6ad5145569bb7bdbcafc02396d92934ed2a6bb2b8bf0da8d262d1145c2079.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some Rivers are Tanks → **F**ollow (As some Rivers are Fishes and all Fishes are Tanks. As whole fishes comes in tanks and has some part common with rivers, therefore it is true.)

(II) Some Ponds are Rivers → Does not follow (As some Ponds are Fishes and some Rivers are Fishes. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (I) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
